**Input.** An instance of the task [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]] with the same $H,|0\rangle,A,\Pi_{\rm good}$ supplied under the prepared-success-subspace access contract of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]]. That contract supplies and charges the uncontrolled calls to $A,A^*,S_0,S_{\rm good}$ and the good/bad projective measurement; no controlled access is used. Also require integers $K,S,J\ge1$.

Set $m_0=0$ and $m_k=2^{k-1}$ for $1\le k\le K$. For each $k=0,\ldots,K$, perform $S$ repetitions: prepare a fresh $A|0\rangle$, apply exactly $m_k$ signed Grover iterates using [[alg-qa-12-amplitude-amplification]], measure the good/bad projective measurement, and record the outcome. Let $h_k$ be the number of good outcomes at scale $k$.

Set $s=2J$ and $\zeta_s=e^{2\pi i/s}$. For an integer $q$, let $\rho_s(q)$ be its least residue in $\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$. For grid labels $j=0,\ldots,J$, put $\theta_j=j\pi/(2J)$ and define the likelihood
$$L_j=\prod_{k=0}^K\sin^{2h_k}((2m_k+1)\theta_j)\cos^{2(S-h_k)}((2m_k+1)\theta_j),$$
where every zeroth power is $1$. For each label $j$ and scale $k=0,\ldots,K$, set
$$r_{kj}=\rho_s((2m_k+1)j),\qquad r'_{kj}=\rho_s(-r_{kj}),$$
and form the rational polynomials
$$U_{kj}(X)=\frac{2-X^{r_{kj}}-X^{r'_{kj}}}{4},\qquad V_{kj}(X)=\frac{2+X^{r_{kj}}+X^{r'_{kj}}}{4}.$$
Put $P_j(X)=\prod_{k=0}^K U_{kj}(X)^{h_k}V_{kj}(X)^{S-h_k}$, treating every zeroth power as $1$. The polynomials $P_j$ are the exact comparison inputs for the likelihoods $L_j$: compare $P_i(\zeta_s)$ and $P_j(\zeta_s)$ using [[lem-qa-13-real-cyclotomic-comparison]], and choose the least label $\widehat j$ attaining the maximum.

Set $E_{\widehat j}(X)=(2-X^{\widehat j}-X^{\rho_s(-\widehat j)})/4$ and return $\widetilde a=E_{\widehat j}(\zeta_s)$, encoded by the pair $(s,E_{\widehat j})$. Each shot uses a fresh state and ordinary measurement. This is a finite-grid likelihood procedure, not a finite-sample $\epsilon,\delta$ guarantee; no such guarantee is asserted here.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $|0\rangle$ a specified unit vector, $A:H\to H$ a supplied unitary, and $\Pi_{\rm good}$ an explicitly supplied orthogonal projection. Put
$$S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad S_{\rm good}=I-2\Pi_{\rm good},\qquad Q=-A S_0A^*S_{\rm good}.$$
Each classical instance has an injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}$ from its declared instance set into $\{0,1\}^*$, with input size $|\operatorname{enc}(z)|$; the promise domain and output obligation are stated for that task. Supplied operator or oracle access is a separate resource declaration.

The success amplitude is $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}A|0\rangle\|^2\in[0,1]$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a\in[0,\pi/2]$. Amplitude estimation returns an algebraically encoded estimate of $a$; its requested accuracy and failure probability are stated separately.

For counting, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and set $N=2^n$ with address basis $\{|x\rangle:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}$ and a Boolean predicate $f$. Set $A=H^{\otimes n}$, $|0\rangle=|0^n\rangle$, $\Pi_{\rm good}=\sum_{f(x)=1}|x\rangle\langle x|$, and $t=|\{x:f(x)=1\}|$. Then the counting amplitude is $a=t/N$. The preparation uses exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamard gates. Access to the controlled membership reflection is a separate explicit resource.

Two phase-estimation access modes are allowed. In the power-query mode, the model supplies each $C(Q^{2^j})$ for $0\le j<m$ as one declared query, with its individual cost recorded. In the repeated-unitary mode the model supplies $C(Q)$ and implements $C(Q^{2^j})$ by $2^j$ sequential calls, for exactly $2^m-1$ controlled-$Q$ calls. In repeated-unitary mode, each controlled-$Q$ call expands as the composite $C(-I)C(A)C(S_0)C(A^*)C(S_{\rm good})$; controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase $C(-I)$ must all be supplied or implemented and charged. In power-query mode each supplied controlled power has its own declared cost vector, including any constituent implementations the model uses. An uncontrolled phase query does not supply any of them. Query, ordinary-gate, state-preparation, measurement, and classical bit costs are separate coordinates.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $|0\rangle\in H$ be a specified unit input vector, let $A:H\to H$ be a supplied measurement-free unitary, and let $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$. The access contract supplies and charges calls to $A$, its inverse $A^\dagger$, the good phase reflection
$
S_{\mathrm{good}}:=I_H-2\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},
$
and the zero-input phase reflection
$
S_0:=I_H-2|0\rangle\langle0|.
$
The signs are part of the contract: $S_{\mathrm{good}}$ is $-I$ on $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ and $+I$ on its orthogonal complement. Reflection about the prepared state is the composite $A S_0 A^\dagger$, with its component calls charged unless a separate direct-reflection access is supplied.

Put $|\psi\rangle=A|0\rangle$ and define the initial success weight
$
a:=\|\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle\|^2\in[0,1].
$
When $a>0$, define $|G\rangle:=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle/\sqrt a$. When $a<1$, define $|B\rangle:=(I_H-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}})|\psi\rangle/\sqrt{1-a}$. These vectors are normalized and lie respectively in the range and kernel of $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$. If $a=0$ or $a=1$, the corresponding zero component is omitted and no vector is normalized from it. With this convention,
$
|\psi\rangle=\sqrt a\,|G\rangle+\sqrt{1-a}\,|B\rangle
$
means the sum of the nonzero component terms. Under the projective measurement $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I_H-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$, the probability of the good outcome is $a$; the finite-dimensional rank-one density and projective-measurement outcome laws are [[thm-qc-unit-vector-projector-is-density]] and [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

The output task may return the conditional quantum state after the good outcome; that state is defined only on a positive-probability branch and is supported in $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ by [[thm-qc-projective-conditional-state]]. A classical output additionally requires $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ to be diagonal in a specified output basis and a costed coherent or ordinary verifier. An arbitrary projection does not supply a classical predicate.

For a $T$-query quantum algorithm [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]] at input length $n$, its **worst-case quantum query cost** is the maximum number of designated oracle calls over all promised instances in $P_n$ and all measurement branches. When $P_n$ is empty, define this cost to be $0$. For nonempty $P_n$, a finite circuit and finite branch sets ensure that this maximum exists; a solver whose branch counts are not uniformly bounded has infinite worst-case query cost. An expected-query bound is the separate quantity defined by [[def-qa-expected-query-cost]].

In the pure query model, ordinary gates outside the oracle calls are uncharged by the query coordinate. If a task also reports gate, preparation, measurement, or classical costs, those are separate coordinates. Bounded-error query cost uses the same worst-case maximum; its success threshold is the per-instance condition in [[def-qa-bounded-error-promise-correctness]], not an average over oracle inputs.

Let $\psi=A|0\rangle$, $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}\psi\|^2$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$. If $0<a<1$, define the unit vectors $G=\Pi_{\rm good}\psi/\sqrt a$ and $B=(I-\Pi_{\rm good})\psi/\sqrt{1-a}$. In the ordered basis $(B,G)$, the Grover iterate $Q$ of [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]] restricts to
$$\begin{pmatrix}\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\\sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its eigenvalues are $e^{2i\theta}$ and $e^{-2i\theta}$, and $\psi=\cos\theta B+\sin\theta G$ has squared overlap $1/2$ with each corresponding normalized eigenvector. At $a=0$, $\psi$ is a $+1$ eigenvector; at $a=1$, it is a $-1$ eigenvector.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

For an integer $s\ge2$, let $\zeta_s=e^{2\pi i/s}$ and let $P,R\in\mathbb Q[X]$ be given coefficient lists such that $P(\zeta_s)$ and $R(\zeta_s)$ are real. There is a terminating deterministic exact procedure to decide which of these two real numbers is larger, or whether they are equal. Its bit-operation cost is charged to the classical cost model; no polynomial bound is asserted.

For each encoded instance length $n$ and explicitly declared public data $p$, a **quantum query algorithm** is a specified finite circuit protocol on its query and work registers, fixed independently of the hidden instance $z$ at fixed $(n,p)$. The hidden encoding labels the oracle instance; it is not supplied as a readable input register. A register is a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with its ordered computational basis; an $r$-qubit register uses the lexicographic bit-string basis, with the first wire most significant ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). The finite promise-computation model [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]] supplies the public-classical-input, zero-initialized ancillary-register, ordered-output-tuple, and final-predicate conventions. Its classical input and terminal predicate receive only the declared public data, not the hidden encoding. Circuit syntax fixes the ordered wires and finite gate list [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], and its denotation fixes the chronological gate composition [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. Registers outside the declared public input start in the zero state unless an explicit preparation interface is supplied. Intermediate measurements and classical feed-forward are represented by finite trees of instrument outcomes and branch-specific unitary operations. All initial states, nonoracle gates and instruments, branch-control rules, and terminal output rules are independent of the hidden instance at fixed $(n,p)$; later operations may depend on observed outcomes. For each instantiated oracle, [[def-qa-finite-branch-output-law]] gives the normalized output law of this tree with its public classical input. The output is interpreted according to the decision bit or search relation in [[def-qa-task-and-promise-domain]].

In the ordinary oracle-only model, hidden-instance dependence enters only through the designated oracle calls. Explicit public parameters and arithmetic inputs remain available when the task declares them. Thus after at most $q$ rounds the scale $L=2^q>4N$ has been reached, so $L^2\ge4N$; the other stopping condition can only make the loop stop earlier. By [F21]–[F22], $y\ne0$ is exactly a nonzero raw estimate test.

For each rough scale $L=2^j$ with $1\le j\le m$, one has $L\theta\le1/5$ and $L^2\le1/(25\theta^2)\le N/25<4N$, because $\theta\ge\sin\theta=\sqrt{t/N}\ge1/\sqrt N$. Thus cutoff cannot occur during these $m$ rounds.

The threshold $T=[20(22/7)^2/\epsilon]L$ is a positive rational. By [F26] and the induction argument in step 1.1, some power of two exceeds $T$, so the doubling loop terminates; its first value $M\ge T$ is the least such power and satisfies $M<2T$. Since $L\ge2$ and $\epsilon\le1$, $T>2$, so $M$ is even and at least $2$, as required by Count and the rounding lemma. Since $22/7>\pi$, $M\ge20\pi^2L/\epsilon$ and $M<40(22/7)^2L/\epsilon$. The rounding step [F24] terminates and makes the integer output explicit; its bit work is covered by [F25].

At each rough scale $L\theta\le1/5$, this and $\sin\theta\le\theta$ yield $P_0(L)\ge\cos^2(L\theta)$ by [F2]. Fresh runs make their zero events independent. If $m\ge1$, then $\theta\le1/10$ and [F8] gives $\prod_{j=1}^m\cos^2(2^j\theta)=[\sin(2^{m+1}\theta)/(2^{m+1}\sin\theta\cos\theta)]^2\ge\cos^2(2/5)$, using $\sin x\ge x\cos x$, $\sin\theta\cos\theta\le\theta$, $2^{m+1}\theta\le2/5$, and the decrease of nonnegative cosine from [F7]. Each Count call uses a fresh preparation; the algorithm uses only the supplied access capabilities in [F21]. It is a finite procedure with exact finite stopping tests and certified final output, but no success or query-cost bound follows from this definition alone.

citations.quote:
**Input.** A Boolean predicate on $N=2^n\ge1$ addresses with an integer $n\ge0$, the fully declared controlled counting access model, and rational $0<\epsilon\le1$.

Set $\ell=0$. Repeatedly increment $\ell$, set $L=2^\ell$, run a fresh Count$(f,L)$, and stop exactly when its label $y$ is nonzero or $L^2\ge4N$. The test $y\ne0$ is an exact finite label test. Initialize $m=0$ and $M=1$; repeatedly increment $m$ and double $M$ while $M<[20(22/7)^2/\epsilon]L$, using exact rational comparison, so that $M=2^m$. Run a fresh Count$(f,M)$ and use [[lem-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding]] to output an integer within $2/3$ of its exact algebraic count estimate. The scale loop returns the least power of two meeting its rational threshold; all scales are powers of two and the multiplier grows as $1/\epsilon$ times $L$.

For a fresh Count run with $L=2^\ell\ge2$ and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt{t/N}$, the QPE label is zero exactly when the raw count estimate is zero. If $0<t<N$, then
$$\Pr(y=0)=\frac{\sin^2(L\theta)}{L^2\sin^2\theta}.$$
For $t=0$ this probability is $1$; when $L=2$ and $0<t<N$ it is $\cos^2\theta$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $|0\rangle$ a specified unit vector, $A:H\to H$ a supplied unitary, and $\Pi_{\rm good}$ an explicitly supplied orthogonal projection. Put
$$S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad S_{\rm good}=I-2\Pi_{\rm good},\qquad Q=-A S_0A^*S_{\rm good}.$$
Each classical instance has an injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}$ from its declared instance set into $\{0,1\}^*$, with input size $|\operatorname{enc}(z)|$; the promise domain and output obligation are stated for that task. Supplied operator or oracle access is a separate resource declaration.

The success amplitude is $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}A|0\rangle\|^2\in[0,1]$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a\in[0,\pi/2]$. Amplitude estimation returns an algebraically encoded estimate of $a$; its requested accuracy and failure probability are stated separately.

For counting, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and set $N=2^n$ with address basis $\{|x\rangle:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}$ and a Boolean predicate $f$. Set $A=H^{\otimes n}$, $|0\rangle=|0^n\rangle$, $\Pi_{\rm good}=\sum_{f(x)=1}|x\rangle\langle x|$, and $t=|\{x:f(x)=1\}|$. Then the counting amplitude is $a=t/N$. The preparation uses exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamard gates. Access to the controlled membership reflection is a separate explicit resource.

Two phase-estimation access modes are allowed. In the power-query mode, the model supplies each $C(Q^{2^j})$ for $0\le j<m$ as one declared query, with its individual cost recorded. In the repeated-unitary mode the model supplies $C(Q)$ and implements $C(Q^{2^j})$ by $2^j$ sequential calls, for exactly $2^m-1$ controlled-$Q$ calls. In repeated-unitary mode, each controlled-$Q$ call expands as the composite $C(-I)C(A)C(S_0)C(A^*)C(S_{\rm good})$; controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase $C(-I)$ must all be supplied or implemented and charged. In power-query mode each supplied controlled power has its own declared cost vector, including any constituent implementations the model uses. An uncontrolled phase query does not supply any of them. Query, ordinary-gate, state-preparation, measurement, and classical bit costs are separate coordinates.

For a $T$-query quantum algorithm [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]] at input length $n$, its **worst-case quantum query cost** is the maximum number of designated oracle calls over all promised instances in $P_n$ and all measurement branches. When $P_n$ is empty, define this cost to be $0$. For nonempty $P_n$, a finite circuit and finite branch sets ensure that this maximum exists; a solver whose branch counts are not uniformly bounded has infinite worst-case query cost. An expected-query bound is the separate quantity defined by [[def-qa-expected-query-cost]].

In the pure query model, ordinary gates outside the oracle calls are uncharged by the query coordinate. If a task also reports gate, preparation, measurement, or classical costs, those are separate coordinates. Bounded-error query cost uses the same worst-case maximum; its success threshold is the per-instance condition in [[def-qa-bounded-error-promise-correctness]], not an average over oracle inputs.

Let $m\ge1$ and $Q=2^m$. Count costs in the ideal continuous-rotation submodel, where each exact controlled phase used by the binary QFT is one gate. If the controlled powers $C(U^{2^j})$, $0\le j<m$, are supplied as one query each, one run uses exactly $m$ controlled-power queries. If the only oracle is $C(U)$, the repeated implementation uses exactly $Q-1$ controlled-$U$ queries. If the supplied controlled-power circuits have ordinary gate counts $C_j$, the unitary gate count after the eigenstate input is provided is
$$\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}C_j+2m+\frac{m(m-1)}2+\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor.$$
The final register measurement reads $m$ bits and is not included in this unitary gate count. No cost-free power construction, fixed finite gate alphabet, uniform family, or state-preparation bound is asserted.

Every complete ordered field $F$ ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) is Archimedean:
for every $x \in F$ there is a natural number $n \ge 1$ with $x < n \cdot 1_F$,
where $n \cdot 1_F$ is the canonical natural of the ordered field $F$
([[def-ordered-field]]). Equivalently, the canonical naturals are cofinal in $F$.

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$. By the recursion theorem ([[thm-recursion]]) applied to
the set $\mathbb{N}$, the starting element $1$ and the function
$f(x) = x \cdot m$ ([[def-nat-multiplication]]), there is a unique function
$\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, written $n \mapsto m^{n}$, with

$$m^{0} = 1, \qquad m^{\sigma(n)} = m^{n} \cdot m \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}).$$

Both the base and the value are natural numbers, so $m^n \in \mathbb{N}$ for all
$m, n$. In particular $m^{1} = m^{0}\cdot m = m$ and $m^{2} = m \cdot m$.

**Why a new item is needed.** [[def-integer-power]] defines $a^{n}$ for a
**real** base $a$, so its value is a real number. The counts on this page,
$\lvert A^{B}\rvert$ and $\lvert\mathcal{P}(A)\rvert$ among them, are natural
numbers, and an identity between them has to be an identity in $\mathbb{N}$. The
two operations are related by clause (d) below and by nothing weaker.

**(a) $0^{0} = 1$ and $0^{n} = 0$ for $n \ge 1$.** The first is the base clause.
For the second, $0^{\sigma(n)} = 0^{n}\cdot 0 = 0$, the clause $x \cdot 0 = 0$
being definitional ([[def-nat-multiplication]]), and every $n \ge 1$ is a
successor.

**(b) $1^{n} = 1$ for every $n$.** Induction: $1^{0} = 1$, and
$1^{\sigma(n)} = 1^{n}\cdot 1 = 1^{n}$ ([[lem-nat-mult-identity]],
[[thm-induction-principle]]).

**(c) $m^{p+q} = m^{p}\,m^{q}$ and $(m p)^{q} = m^{q} p^{q}$.** Both by induction
on $q$, using associativity and commutativity of multiplication
([[lem-nat-mult-associative]], [[lem-nat-mult-commutative]]). For the first, at
$q = 0$ we have $m^{p+0} = m^{p} = m^{p}\cdot 1 = m^{p}m^{0}$, and
$m^{p+\sigma(q)} = m^{\sigma(p+q)} = m^{p+q}\cdot m = (m^{p}m^{q})\cdot m = m^{p}\,m^{\sigma(q)}$,
using $p + \sigma(q) = \sigma(p+q)$ ([[def-nat-addition]]). For the second, at
$q = 0$ both sides are $1$, and
$(mp)^{\sigma(q)} = (mp)^{q}(mp) = m^{q}p^{q}mp = m^{\sigma(q)}p^{\sigma(q)}$.

**(d) The bridge into $\mathbb{R}$.** With $\iota : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$
the canonical natural ([[def-canonical-natural]]) and $x^{n}$ the integer power
of [[def-integer-power]],

$$\iota\big(m^{n}\big) = \iota(m)^{n} \qquad (m, n \in \mathbb{N}).$$

Induction on $n$: at $n = 0$ both sides are $1$, since $\iota(1) = 1$; and
$\iota(m^{\sigma(n)}) = \iota(m^{n}\cdot m) = \iota(m^{n})\,\iota(m) = \iota(m)^{n}\iota(m) = \iota(m)^{\sigma(n)}$,
the second equality being the multiplicativity of $\iota$ (clause 0 of
[[lem-nat-finite-sum-laws-and-the-canonical-embedding]]) and the last the
recursion clause of [[def-integer-power]].

**(e) $m^{n}$ is a constant product.** $m^{n} = \prod_{k<n} m$, the
$\mathbb{N}$-valued product of the constant list
([[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]]). Induction: at $n = 0$ both sides are $1$,
and $\prod_{k<\sigma(n)} m = \big(\prod_{k<n} m\big)\cdot m = m^{n}\cdot m = m^{\sigma(n)}$.

Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. If $0 \in S$ and $\sigma(n) \in S$ whenever $n \in S$, then $S = \mathbb{N}$. Equivalently (property form): if a property $P$ satisfies $P(0)$ and ($P(n) \Rightarrow P(\sigma(n))$) for all $n$, then $P(n)$ holds for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. This is the induction principle, the basis of proof by induction.

Let $\psi=A|0\rangle$, $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}\psi\|^2$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$. If $0<a<1$, define the unit vectors $G=\Pi_{\rm good}\psi/\sqrt a$ and $B=(I-\Pi_{\rm good})\psi/\sqrt{1-a}$. In the ordered basis $(B,G)$, the Grover iterate $Q$ of [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]] restricts to
$$\begin{pmatrix}\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\\sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its eigenvalues are $e^{2i\theta}$ and $e^{-2i\theta}$, and $\psi=\cos\theta B+\sin\theta G$ has squared overlap $1/2$ with each corresponding normalized eigenvector. At $a=0$, $\psi$ is a $+1$ eigenvector; at $a=1$, it is a $-1$ eigenvector.
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$. If $Q\theta=t\in\mathbb Z$, then $t\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, phase estimation returns $y=t$ with probability $1$, and every other output has probability $0$.

**Input.** A Boolean predicate $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, an explicitly supplied controlled membership reflection for $S_{\rm good}$, a power of two $M=2^m\ge2$, and the other controlled accesses in [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]].

Prepare $N^{-1/2}\sum_x|x\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$, run the $m$-qubit QPE circuit for $Q$ with $M=2^m$ labels, measure $y$, and output the exact algebraic fraction estimate $\widetilde a=\sin^2(\pi y/M)$ and count estimate $\widetilde t=N\widetilde a$. For $M\ge4$ this is the QFT amplitude-estimation circuit of [[alg-qa-13-phase-estimation-amplitude-estimation]]; for $M=2$, use its one-phase-qubit QPE circuit directly, without invoking the $M\ge4$ error theorem. The fraction and count are real-valued algebraic outputs; integer rounding is optional postprocessing. The controlled membership reflection is an explicit access requirement. In repeated-unitary mode each controlled $Q$ call charges one controlled membership reflection; in power-query mode each supplied controlled power carries its declared cost vector, including any membership-reflection implementations it uses. Neither access mode is inferred from the bare phase oracle $|x\rangle\mapsto(-1)^{f(x)}$.

derivations.claim: If $t=N$, [F7] gives phase $1/2$; at the first rough scale $L=2$, [F9] and [F8] give label $y=1\ne0$, so the loop stops at $L=2$. For $0<t<N$, $\sin^2\theta=t/N$, and [F2] gives $P_0(L)\le1/(L^2\sin^2\theta)=N/(tL^2)$. Once $L\ge18\pi\sqrt{N/t}$, this is at most $1/(324\pi^2)<1/4$.

Suppose $0<t<N$ and put $X=18\pi\sqrt{N/t}$. Choose a natural $q>X$ by [F6]. Induction using the natural-power recursion gives $2^q\ge q+1$, so a dyadic scale exceeds $X$; scanning the rough scales in order reaches a first $L_*\ge X$. Its preceding scale is smaller than $X$, hence $L_*<2X=36\pi\sqrt{N/t}$. By [F5], a rough Count at scale $L$ costs $L-1\le L$ controlled-$Q$ calls. The rough query costs below $L_*$ sum to less than $2L_*$. If the loop reaches $L_*$, each later zero outcome has conditional probability at most $1/4$ by step 1.1; reaching the $j$th later scale costs at most $2^jL_*$ and has probability at most $4^{-j}$. Hence the expected tail is bounded by $L_*\sum_{j\ge0}(1/2)^j=2L_*$. If the cutoff occurs before $L_*$, it only removes terms from these upper bounds. Thus the expected rough cost is $O(\sqrt{N/t})$. If $L$ is the actual stopping scale, its final rough Count costs $L-1\ge L/2$ calls since $L\ge2$, so $\mathbb E L$ is at most twice the expected rough query cost and is also $O(\sqrt{N/t})$.

The final dyadic $M$ is less than twice its threshold, so $M=O(L/\epsilon)$. By [F5], the final Count uses $M-1$ calls; for $0<t<N$, the bound on $\mathbb E L$ in step 2.1 therefore gives $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{N/t})$ expected final controlled-$Q$ calls, while the rough term is absorbed because $\epsilon\le1$. If $t=N$, step 1.1 gives $L=2$, so the rough cost is one call and the final size is $M=O(1/\epsilon)$, matching $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{N/t})$. If $t=0$, the cutoff scale lies in $[2\sqrt N,4\sqrt N)$, the geometric rough-call sum is $O(\sqrt N)$, and the final schedule uses $M=O(\sqrt N/\epsilon)$ calls by [F5]. Thus the stated zero-case cost retains the $\epsilon$ factor.

Each repeated controlled-$Q$ call contains exactly one controlled $S_{\rm good}$ factor by [F3]; [F4] keeps that query count separate from controlled $A/A^*$ and other gates. Thus the stated membership-reflection and resource counts follow.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

For $M=2^m\ge4$, repeated controlled-$Q$ access uses exactly $M-1$ controlled-$Q$ applications in one run; each expands to one call each to controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase. Supplied controlled-power access uses exactly $m$ power queries and reports their separate costs. With fixed success probability, additive amplitude error $\epsilon\in(0,1]$ is obtained with $M=\Theta(1/\epsilon)$, hence $O(1/\epsilon)$ repeated controlled-$Q$ calls; state preparation, ordinary gates, and classical encoding are separate costs.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $|0\rangle$ a specified unit vector, $A:H\to H$ a supplied unitary, and $\Pi_{\rm good}$ an explicitly supplied orthogonal projection. Put
$$S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad S_{\rm good}=I-2\Pi_{\rm good},\qquad Q=-A S_0A^*S_{\rm good}.$$
Each classical instance has an injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}$ from its declared instance set into $\{0,1\}^*$, with input size $|\operatorname{enc}(z)|$; the promise domain and output obligation are stated for that task. Supplied operator or oracle access is a separate resource declaration.

The success amplitude is $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}A|0\rangle\|^2\in[0,1]$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a\in[0,\pi/2]$. Amplitude estimation returns an algebraically encoded estimate of $a$; its requested accuracy and failure probability are stated separately.

For counting, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and set $N=2^n$ with address basis $\{|x\rangle:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}$ and a Boolean predicate $f$. Set $A=H^{\otimes n}$, $|0\rangle=|0^n\rangle$, $\Pi_{\rm good}=\sum_{f(x)=1}|x\rangle\langle x|$, and $t=|\{x:f(x)=1\}|$. Then the counting amplitude is $a=t/N$. The preparation uses exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamard gates. Access to the controlled membership reflection is a separate explicit resource.

Two phase-estimation access modes are allowed. In the power-query mode, the model supplies each $C(Q^{2^j})$ for $0\le j<m$ as one declared query, with its individual cost recorded. In the repeated-unitary mode the model supplies $C(Q)$ and implements $C(Q^{2^j})$ by $2^j$ sequential calls, for exactly $2^m-1$ controlled-$Q$ calls. In repeated-unitary mode, each controlled-$Q$ call expands as the composite $C(-I)C(A)C(S_0)C(A^*)C(S_{\rm good})$; controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase $C(-I)$ must all be supplied or implemented and charged. In power-query mode each supplied controlled power has its own declared cost vector, including any constituent implementations the model uses. An uncontrolled phase query does not supply any of them. Query, ordinary-gate, state-preparation, measurement, and classical bit costs are separate coordinates.

derivations.claim: Let the target be one-dimensional and compare $U=I$ with $U'=-I$. An uncontrolled call to $U'$ differs from an uncontrolled call to $U$ by a scalar phase on the target, so every fixed sequence of uncontrolled calls has the same physical outcome probabilities after any final measurement; global phase cancels from a vector's rank-one projector.

On a control qubit, however, $C(I)=I$ while $C(-I)=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)=Z$. On input $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, the first returns $|+\rangle$ and the second returns $| -\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$; a computational-basis-independent $X$-basis measurement distinguishes them with certainty. Thus controlled access contains information absent from the uncontrolled phase-equivalence class.

The cost theorem counts supplied controlled powers or repetitions of controlled Q only under the corresponding access declaration. Repeated-unitary mode charges its controlled-Q constituents; power-query mode charges each supplied power and its declared cost vector, including any implementation constituents. The witness proves that neither mode’s controlled access is free from a bare uncontrolled oracle.
